description: kpexec is a kubernetes cli that runs commands in a container with high privileges.

summary.one_liner: kpexec is a Kubernetes CLI that runs commands in a target container with elevated privileges, without SSH, by launching a privileged helper pod on the same node.
summary.what_it_does: kpexec looks up the target pod through the Kubernetes API and finds its node. It then creates a privileged "cnsenter" pod on that node, which joins the target container's IPC, UTS, PID, network and mount namespaces. The cnsenter pod gets the container's PID and root directory through the Container Runtime Interface (CRI) and runs the requested command there. A tools mode (-T) adds debugging tools into the target container when they are missing. A cnsenter garbage collector (--cnsenter-gc) removes leftover helper pods. kpexec uses kubectl internally, so kubectl and a kubeconfig must be set up first.
use_cases: debug a pod with network or host-level privileges the container lacks
run commands in a container without SSH access
add debugging tools to a container that does not have them
exec into a pod's namespaces from the node
clean up leftover debug helper pods in a cluster
how_to_run: Install kubectl and configure a kubeconfig for your cluster
Download the kpexec binary for your OS and architecture, or install via Homebrew: brew install ssup2/tap/kpexec
Run a command in a pod: kpexec mypod -- date
Get an interactive shell: kpexec -it mypod -c bash-container -- bash
Enable tools mode: kpexec -it -T mypod -c bash-container -- bash
notable: Runs commands with higher privileges than kubectl exec, which keeps the container's own privileges
Tools mode injects debugging utilities into containers that lack them
Works with containerd, CRI-O and Docker runtimes
Available as a kubectl plugin via Krew under the name pexec
Supports amd64 and arm64 CPU architectures
caveats: The cnsenter pod needs hostPID, privileged mode and hostPath, which some clusters may restrict
Requires a working kubectl installation and kubeconfig
Shell autocompletion does not work when installed via Krew
